original_value: This paper deals with the design of an electronic device aimed at the detection and characterization of volatile chemical substances, that is, an electronic nose (e-nose). We pursue the development of a versatile, multipurpose e-nose that can be employed for a wide variety of applications, can integrate heterogeneous sensing technologies, and can offer a mechanism to be customized for different requirements. To that end, we contribute with a fully configurable and decentralized e-nose architecture based on self-contained and intelligent sensor boards (i.e., modules). This design allows for the integration not only of heterogeneous gas sensor technologies, like MOX and AEC sensors, but also of other components, such as GPS or Bluetooth, for a total of up to 127 individual modules. We describe an implementation of a fully operative prototype as an illustrative example of its potential for sensor networks, mobile robotics, and wearable technologies, each using different combinations of sensors.

result.paraphrase: This paper presents the design of an electronic device for detecting and characterizing volatile chemical substances: an electronic nose (e-nose). Our goal is to develop a versatile, multipurpose e-nose suitable for a broad range of applications, capable of integrating heterogeneous sensing technologies, and customizable to different requirements. To achieve this, we propose a fully configurable, decentralized e-nose architecture built from self-contained, intelligent sensor boards, or modules. The design supports not only heterogeneous gas sensor technologies such as MOX and AEC sensors, but also other components like GPS or Bluetooth, for as many as 127 individual modules in total. We also describe a fully functional prototype as an illustrative example of its potential for sensor networks, mobile robotics, and wearable technologies, each employing different sensor combinations.
